text:
ashwin: quick smoke on Scout7b int4. ran 2k random longform RAG docs (multidoc, ~1200 tokens avg). cost down ~24% vs our int8 build, p50 latency ~10% lower, but quality drop on our primary signals (R-L -7%, relevance signal -6%).

maya: can you paste the slice breakdown? which queries trigger the drop?

ashwin: mostly long context multi-doc and factuality checks. short QA <256 tokens looks fine. sample: `slice=multidoc_long; n=600; rl_drop=9%`

kevin: that's .. larger than I'd expect. was this pure static int4 or mixed-precision?

ashwin: static int4 w/ per-channel quant, no outlier clipping. we also tried int4-calib (layerwise) which reduced rl drop to ~4% but cost savings went to ~18%.

leah: any latency tail impact? p95?

ashwin: p95 +3% on int4-static (weird, KV cache miss pattern on long sequences). int4-calib p95 ~= baseline. p50 improved across both.

ops-bot: deploy job #4821 started -> canary to staging cluster (scout7b-int4)

maya: unit econ numbers pls (tokens/sec, $/1M tokens) for baseline int8 vs int4-calib vs int4-static

ashwin: baseline int8: 120k tokens/s GPU pool (effective), est $4.6 / 1M tokens. int4-static: 158k tokens/s, est $3.5 / 1M. int4-calib: 150k tokens/s, est $3.8 / 1M. (these include infra overhead & batching)

kevin: interesting. so int4-calib is a middle ground: ~17% cost save vs int8 with smaller quality hit.

leah: product/GTN question: can we accept ~4% RL drop for some routes? sophie? @sophie

sophie: for GTN chat summarization no, we need <2% RL degradation on our primary corpus. for search rerank we can tolerate up to ~6% if recall stays stable.

maya: suggests routing policy: keep int8 for routes flagged as "high-fidelity" (multi-doc, >512 tokens, rerank/evals), use int4-calib for low-fidelity chat completions and ephemeral tasks.

kevin: we can implement a token-based router: if request.tokens_est > 512 OR req.type in ["rerank","longform"], route to scout7b-int8, else scout7b-int4-calib. fallback chain to scout7b-int8 on low-signal outputs.

ashwin: quick config snippet i used for the smoke:
```
route:
  - name: longform-fallback
    match: req.tokens_est > 512
    primary: scout7b-int4-static
    fallback: scout7b-int8
    qos: high
```

maya: hmm that primary seems risky. swap primary to int4-calib for lower RL hit.

ashwin: ack, updated locally. also flagging an eval gap: our fidelity checks didn't include adversarial hallucination prompts. need to run targeted slices.

leah: action items?

ashwin: 1) run adversarial-affecting-slices (2k prompts) on int4-calib vs int8 by EOD tomorrow.
2) run a 24h canary with token-based router in staging (10% traffic).
3) attach regression alerts for RL/relevance (>2% drop) and hallucination spike.

kevin: i can wire the canary routing, ops-bot will handle infra toggles.

deploy-bot: canary created: canary-id=can-202352, traffic=10%, start=now

maya: also add cost-savings dashboard by route and per-token unit econ so GTN/product can model tradeoffs.

sophie: +1. please include sample UX impact note for GTN: e.g., "expected summary quality delta -3 to -5 pts" per model/route.

ashwin: will draft a mini scorecard: metrics (R-L, relevance, hallucination rate, p50/p95 latency, $/1M tokens) and include n-slices. posting in #eng-ml after runs. :thumbsup:

leah: nice. if canary looks clean we can ship int4-calib for low-fidelity routes next week. hold high-fidelity routes on int8 until product okays.

maya: thanks all — ping me if you need extra GTN sims.

kevin: logging results to /evals/scout7b/3522223333/ — will update thread when canary completes.

ashwin: thanks — closing loop here, will post the scorecard + raw slice artifacts.
